subject: Observability export validation for private deployment - Greenfield Health
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Dave Lawson <dave.lawson@itvendor.com>, security@greenfieldhealth.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability export validation for private deployment - Greenfield Health

Hi Dave / Greenfield SecOps,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. As we prepare the private deployment package for your VPC/on-prem environment, we want to validate a few concrete points about log/metric export and tracing hooks so our engineers can build the right handoff and request the right infra approvals.

Quick asks:
- SIEM: do you expect a push (Redwood->Greenfield Splunk HEC / syslog receiver) or will you pull from S3/FTP? If push, please confirm host/port, TLS requirements, and any mutual TLS certs.
- Egress: are there allowed outbound IPs (or a NAT) we should use, or is connectivity strictly peered? Any blocked ports (e.g., 8088)?
- Tracing: preferred ingestion protocol (OTLP/gRPC/HTTP), sampler expectations (sample rates), and whether trace context must be preserved by any forwarding layer.
- Retention & batching: retention window for logs/metrics, and acceptable batch size/frequency — we can tune buffering to meet retention and latency SLOs.

I attached a short options summary (redwood-private-telemetry-options.pdf) describing three patterns we commonly propose: sidecar forwarder (recommended for air-gapped), VPC egress via a managed NAT + HEC endpoint, and S3 export + scheduled ingestion. We'll propose a default after your responses.

Can we also lock a 45-minute technical call tomorrow morning (May 10) with your IT ops and SecOps to walk through firewall rules and cert exchange?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
[attachment: redwood-private-telemetry-options.pdf (PDF)]

From: Dave Lawson <dave.lawson@itvendor.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: security@greenfieldhealth.com, itops@greenfieldhealth.com
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 18:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability export validation for private deployment - Greenfield Health

Hi Camila — thanks for the checklist. High level answers below and attached is our SIEM requirements workbook.

- SIEM mode: we prefer a push to our Splunk HEC collector for near-real-time logs. HEC endpoint: https://10.20.30.5:8088/services/collector (internal only). HEC token auth; mutual TLS desired for metadata-forwarding services.
- Egress/connectivity: Our on-prem clusters are isolated; we allow inbound from partner IPs via explicit firewall rules. No outbound internet (no NAT) from the cluster except to our internal proxy (10.20.30.1).
- Ports: 8088 (HEC) open from designated partners; 4317 (OTLP/gRPC) allowed to internal tracing collector at 10.20.30.7:4317.
- Tracing protocol: OTLP/gRPC preferred. We require trace-parent propagation and prefer a 10% sampling rate for service-level traces, 100% for error spans.
- Retention & batching: Logs are retained 365 days in Splunk; we prefer smaller batches to reduce memory pressure on our collector (max batch 200 events or 5s flush).

Attached: Greenfield_SIEM_requirements.xlsx (contains cert exchange process and our partner onboarding checklist). Also: we require a signed AUP and a network security contact for cert pinning.

We can do the technical call tomorrow May 10 at 09:00 PT.

—Dave
Dave Lawson
Senior Integrations Engineer, Systems Integrations
IT Vendor Partners (contracted by Greenfield Health)
[attachment: Greenfield_SIEM_requirements.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Dave Lawson <dave.lawson@itvendor.com>, security@greenfieldhealth.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 May 2028 20:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability export validation for private deployment - Greenfield Health

Thanks Dave — very helpful. I skimmed the spreadsheet and flagged the cert exchange and partner IP list items we need to coordinate with legal and infra.

Proposal summary (we'll expand on the call):
1) Sidecar forwarder (recommended): deploy a lightweight forwarder alongside Redwood Private workloads that posts to your internal HEC and OTLP collectors over the private network. Benefits: no internet egress, mTLS termination close to the source, low latency. Tradeoffs: requires deployment access in the cluster and a brief infra window for firewall rules.
2) VPC egress route to internal proxy: Redwood uses managed NAT to reach your proxy (10.20.30.1) and the proxy forwards to Splunk/OTLP. Benefits: minimal agent footprint. Tradeoffs: more moving pieces; proxy reliability becomes critical.
3) S3 export + pull: less ideal given near-real-time needs and your 365-day retention.

For the morning call: I'll include a short runbook for cert exchange and a clear checklist for firewall rules. Can you confirm which partner IP(s) Greenfield will whitelist? Also: do you require our forwarder to present a client cert per connection or will a single token suffice for the initial pilot?

Next internal steps: looping in Lauren and Rishi to validate compliance requirements and confirm we can supply the evidence bundle (CA certs, audit logs, and data flow diagrams) for your security team. Monica, can you help prepare the SOC2 artifacts we typically use for this onboarding?

Camila

Nice write-up Camila. Quick internal guidance before the call:

- Preference: sidecar forwarder for the pilot. It minimizes attack surface and makes certificate rotation straightforward.
- Tracing: require OTLP/gRPC, 10% default sampling, set error spans to 100%. Ensure forwarder preserves W3C trace-context (traceparent).
- Evidence: we need to bundle (a) data flow diagram showing no internet egress, (b) forwarder config sample, (c) CA cert chain and pinning instructions. Monica, please assemble a minimal evidence bundle we can hand to Greenfield during the pilot.
- SLA note: flag that in Dedicated/Dedicated-Private the forwarder can run on a dedicated infra node for throughput isolation.

I'll join the 09:00 PT call.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: monica.patel@redwood.ai <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 08:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability export validation for private deployment - Greenfield Health

Thanks — I'll prepare the evidence bundle and the minimal SOC2-related extracts for the call. Planned contents:
- CA cert chain and cert rotation plan (PDF)
- Forwarder config sample (YAML) with OTLP endpoints and batching policy
- Data flow diagram (PNG) and a short AUP draft for partner onboarding
- List of audit logs we can export (authz, ingestion, config changes) + retention policy

Also: please confirm whether we should redact client IP addresses in logs by default for PHI sensitivity — Greenfield is a healthcare customer, so default should be conservative. I'll mark redaction as a configurable toggle in the forwarder.

I'll upload everything to the shared Drive folder and paste the link in the call notes.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
